diego: Heads-up, bringing up ml-model-7b-v2 in the eval harness and seeing a tokenizer mismatch vs the serving runtime. token counts for the same prompt differ (sometimes by +1).

maya: repro steps? config used?

diego: quick repro:```\nfrom transforms import Tokenizer\ntok = Tokenizer.from_pretrained('ml-model-7b-v2-tokenizer')\nprompt = 'Translate to French:\nHello world!'\nprint(tok.encode(prompt))\nprint(len(tok.encode(prompt)))\n```\nOn the runtime (serving) the model gets 17 tokens, in harness it's 18. Looks like an extra empty token after newline.

sam: is that the HF tokenizer vs our internal sentencepiece conversion? we had a mismatch patch last quarter that added a special newline token.

diego: yeah i'm seeing the special token in the vocab: `<NL_PAD>` — but harness pipeline does `prettify_prompt` which inserts `\n\n` in some templates. combine that with add_special_tokens=True -> double count.

jen: this is causing failing eval runners (compare_tokens metric). CI shows a failing param for the runner:```\nE       assert 0.941 == 0.948\nE        +  where 0.941 = compare_tokens(pred, ref)\nE        +    where pred = '[...token list...]'\nE        +    and ref = '[...token list...]'\nE       tests/evals/test_runner.py:84: AssertionError\n```\n
luis: quick options: 1) normalize in harness (strip extra NLs) 2) switch tokenizer call to `add_special_tokens=False` then manually add tokens for model runtime parity 3) change metric to ignore leading/trailing special NL tokens.

maya: prefer (3) + (2) as a short-term since changing prompts across templates is riskier. we should define metric semantics explicitly: `normalized_token_match` which excludes leading/trailing special tokens and collapses contiguous NL tokens.

sam: ok. also saw CI job for the eval-runner failing because pytest param ids changed when we started injecting `chat_role` into template metadata. the runner expects positional args, now gets kwargs -> test harness mis-params.

diego: repro for the param bug:```\n# tests/evals/test_runner.py\n@pytest.mark.parametrize('prompt,expected', [\n  ({'text': 'hi'}, 'OK'),\n])\n# but runner now calls run(prompt=..., meta={'chat_role': 'user'})\n```\nSo pytest shows mismatched call signature in the fixture.

jen: short term: pin older runner fixture in CI for the branch. long term: make runner accept both positional and kwargs. I'll add a small wrapper.

ci-bot: Failed job: https://ci.redwood.internal/agent/6789 — pytest tests/evals/test_runner.py::test_stream_vs_sync — logs attached.

diego: I'm going to open two PRs: one for the metric change + unit tests for `normalized_token_match`, and one to change tokenizer calls in the harness to `add_special_tokens=False` + explicit runtime token glue so we mirror serving.

sam: dashboard note: reporting dashboard (evals -> comparisons) expects `model_short_name` column. onboarding script writes `model_id` only, so new model shows as blank. simple fix in reporters.py:```\n# reporters.py\nrow['model_short_name'] = model_id.split(':')[-1]\n```\n
luis: also watch quantization experiments: some q4 variants change tokenization slightly due to tokenizer config baked into conversion steps. add a CI gate for quantized-onboard: `tests/onboard/test_tokenizer_parity.py` that compares `encode(prompt)` between harness and serving binary.

maya: good. action items: 1) diego PRs for metric + tokenizer change 2) jen wraps runner to accept kwargs (CI hotfix) 3) sam patches reporter for dashboard 4) luis adds quantization parity test.

diego: will draft PRs now, linking the failing job and a small repro gist: https://gist.internal/abc123

jen: if anyone needs me to review earlier today ping in this thread. I'll triage the CI hotfix first.

sam: thx, keeping this short — good find, diego. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: NOTE: job retrigger recommended after PRs land.
